text:
erin: Heads-up — I'm drafting a proposal for a per-tenant 'beta routing' UX for Dedicated customers. The idea: let an enterprise tenant opt a portion of their traffic into a canary slice with optional isolation constraints and automatic fallback. WIP below, looking for quick feedback.

matt: SG. Do we want a console-only flow or an API-first model (so infra can automate ramps)?

erin: Thinking both. Console for product teams to do one-off bets, API for infra/CD to automate ramps. Proposed minimal API payload: 

```json
POST /rollouts
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "model": "redwood-v2.1",
  "split_percent": 5,
  "isolation": "soft", // soft|hard
  "max_qps": 200,
  "fallback_policy": "auto-divert"
}
```

tanya: Need clear defs: soft isolation = logical separation (namespaces, per-tenant cache keys). Hard isolation = dedicated pools (no co-tenancy). Also clarify SLO mixing rules — hard isolation must guarantee no baseline traffic interference.

kevin: Telemetry needs to be per-slice. We should emit labels: tenant_id, rollout_id, slice=canary|control, and origin (console|api). That lets dashboards filter and alert on canary-specific SLIs (p99, error_rate, cost_per_token).

erin: +1. Also propose automatic rollback trigger config: e.g., "rollback_on": ["p99 > 500ms for 5m", "error_rate > 1% for 3m"]. Platform default = conservative. Customers can tighten.

sylvia: Question: who owns the fallback decision? Platform default should do auto-divert to baseline. But customers may want to opt out (e.g., they accept instability during experiments). How do we surface waivers in the console?

matt: Platform owns default safety. Console shows a checkbox "allow unsafe canary" with audit and required approval. API has flag allow_waiver=true (only usable with enterprise role).

deploy-bot: deploy-check: canary schema validation against tenant quotas: PASS.

tanya: One more ops note: KV/LM cache isolation. Soft isolation = prefix per tenant+rollout, still shared pool; hard = dedicated cache instances or dedicated pod pool with separate KV stores. Recommend soft for small splits, hard for >25% or if tenant requires regulatory isolation.

kevin: Also sticky routing for A/B tests: need a deterministic hashing key (customer_id or session_id) so experiments are consistent. Must document preferred key and how we handle multiple concurrent rollouts for same tenant.

erin: Drafting a short RFC to capture: API schema, console mockups, telemetry labels, cache isolation modes, fallback rules, and audit/approval UX. Action items: @matt own telemetry schema + dashboard mock, @tanya vet cache isolation proposal and thresholds, @kevin draft fallback engine behavior and SLA mixing rules. I'll create RFC and share.

matt: 👍 I'll start a prometheus/panels sketch with per-rollout panels (qps, p50/p90/p99, errors, cost/token).

sylvia: Ops will also want runbook snippets for manual rollback and steps to escalate if auto-divert fails.

erin: thanks — will include runbook draft in RFC. If nobody objects, I'll open RFC later today and tag you all. :sparkles:

matt: :eyes: watching for the RFC.

tanya: No objections from ops side.

kevin: fine by me. small nit: ensure the API error returns include rollout_id for easy tracing.

erin: good call — will add rollout_id in 202 responses and in tracing headers.

sylvia: thanks, will prep runbook checklist.
